corrections.text: The headline says Google "Caps One Listed Service per Project". Google's documentation says a spend cap budget is scoped to "a single Google Cloud project and a single eligible service within the specified project" (the FAQ: "Spend cap budgets can only be set on one project and one service at a time"), so the phrase describes the scope of one cap. The cited pages do not say a project can hold only one capped service; the FAQ's deduplication policy prevents only "more than one budget with the same scope".

The article says that on Google "new requests to the capped service stop while persistent resources keep running". Google's general-availability post, which the article cites, also says "Provisioned Throughput is never halted; requests using reserved capacity will continue to run", and InfoQ states the same, so not all new usage of a capped service stops.

The article gives The Register's report as "published 05:52 UTC", which is the time the page prints. The page's machine-readable published_time is 2026-09-18T04:52:40.000Z, an hour earlier; the date, September 18, is the same on either basis.
